selector: :is(button, [role=button]):not([aria-busy=true], [aria-busy=true]:not(input, select, textarea, html, form) *, details.dropdown > summary + ul *, nav[aria-label=breadcrumb] ul li a):not(button.secondary[class*="femto-background-"])
reason: 2.1.1 sizes a button or [role=button] link to its content, so a label holding a long unbroken string, such as a URL, hash or ID, sets the button's width and pushes it past its container: 1345px in a 300px box in Chrome. The root's inherited overflow-wrap: break-word never breaks the word, because nothing narrows the button. femto gives button and [role=button] max-width: 100% through a zero-specificity rule, so the label breaks inside the container. Short and multi-word buttons are unchanged when their container is at least as wide as the label's longest word; in a narrower one, such as a .grid cell, a word now breaks inside the button instead of the button overflowing the cell. The rule skips a busy button and the contents of a busy element other than html and form, and dropdown menus, because loading.css and dropdown.css give them white-space: nowrap, so a cap would only push the label past the button's edge; it also keeps the dropdown's negative-margin link items at their width. Buttons in a busy form or a busy html are still capped, since loading.css leaves those wrapping. Breadcrumb links are skipped because of their negative margin-inline-start: their item is sized to the link, and the cap would cut the link by that margin and break its label. Inputs and ::file-selector-button are not matched, since their text cannot wrap. On fixtures without long labels, the only computed difference is max-width and its logical alias max-inline-size: none in 2.1.1, 100% in femto.
